Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out whether any
feature overlaps, leaves a gap, is a sliver, duplicates another, or
(for lines) dangles unconnected.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

This is diagnosis only, not repair — fixing a topology error almost
always requires a human decision (see the
[full article](/posts/topology-errors.html) for why), so there's no
"Fix" step here, just the report and a map to inspect it on.

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable check
using GeoPandas/Shapely underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/topology-errors.html) for the actual code,
editable and explained one check at a time.

Gap and sliver aren't absolute properties of a dataset — they depend
on a judgment call. **Sliver threshold** (compactness, 0-1): how thin
counts as "not a real shape" — lower catches only thinner slivers.
**Gap search distance** (degrees): how close two features need to be
before a gap between them counts — larger finds gaps further apart.

*First run loads the Python engine — expect about a minute. Instant
after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

{{< webgeods-tool topology-tool id=topo-root min-height=820px >}}

```{.webgeods-python #topology-diagnose-py .tool-cell}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
#| helper: read_upload
#| inject: [sliverThreshold, gapProximity]
import math
from shapely.geometry import mapping

def geom_family(gdf):
    types = set(gdf.geometry.geom_type)
    if types <= {"Polygon", "MultiPolygon"}:
        return "polygon"
    if types <= {"LineString", "MultiLineString"}:
        return "line"
    if types <= {"Point", "MultiPoint"}:
        return "point"
    return "mixed"

def check_overlap(gdf):
    n = len(gdf)
    results = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            gi, gj = gdf.geometry.iloc[i], gdf.geometry.iloc[j]
            if gi.overlaps(gj):
                area = gi.intersection(gj).area
                results[i].append(("overlap", j, area))
                results[j].append(("overlap", i, area))
    return results

def check_duplicate(gdf):
    n = len(gdf)
    results = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if gdf.geometry.iloc[i].equals(gdf.geometry.iloc[j]):
                results[i].append(("duplicate", j, 0))
                results[j].append(("duplicate", i, 0))
    return results

def check_sliver(gdf, compactness_threshold=0.15):
    results = [[] for _ in range(len(gdf))]
    for i, geom in enumerate(gdf.geometry):
        perim = geom.length
        area = geom.area
        if perim > 0:
            compactness = 4 * math.pi * area / (perim ** 2)
            if compactness < compactness_threshold:
                results[i].append(("sliver", None, compactness))
    return results

def check_gap(gdf, min_area=1e-6, proximity=0.06):
    n = len(gdf)
    gaps = []
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            gi, gj = gdf.geometry.iloc[i], gdf.geometry.iloc[j]
            if gi.overlaps(gj):
                continue
            if gi.equals(gj):
                continue
            if gi.distance(gj) > proximity:
                continue
            pair_union = gi.union(gj)
            gap_geom = pair_union.convex_hull.difference(pair_union)
            if not gap_geom.is_empty:
                parts = gap_geom.geoms if hasattr(gap_geom, "geoms") else [gap_geom]
                for part in parts:
                    if part.area > min_area:
                        gaps.append(part)
    return gaps

def check_dangle(gdf, tolerance=1e-9):
    endpoints = []
    for i, geom in enumerate(gdf.geometry):
        coords = list(geom.coords)
        endpoints.append((i, "start", coords[0]))
        endpoints.append((i, "end", coords[-1]))
    results = [[] for _ in range(len(gdf))]
    for i, which, (x, y) in endpoints:
        connected = False
        for j, which2, (x2, y2) in endpoints:
            if j == i:
                continue
            if ((x - x2) ** 2 + (y - y2) ** 2) ** 0.5 <= tolerance:
                connected = True
                break
        if not connected:
            results[i].append(("dangle", which, 0))
    return results

def detect_and_check(gdf, sliver_threshold=0.15, gap_proximity=0.06):
    family = geom_family(gdf)
    n = len(gdf)
    per_feature = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    extra_features = []

    dup = check_duplicate(gdf)
    for i in range(n):
        per_feature[i].extend(dup[i])

    if family == "polygon":
        ov = check_overlap(gdf)
        sl = check_sliver(gdf, compactness_threshold=sliver_threshold)
        for i in range(n):
            per_feature[i].extend(ov[i])
            per_feature[i].extend(sl[i])
        for gap_geom in check_gap(gdf, proximity=gap_proximity):
            extra_features.append({
                "type": "Feature",
                "properties": {
                    "name": "gap", "error_type": "gap", "has_error": True,
                    "partner": "", "metric": round(gap_geom.area, 6), "severity": "warning"
                },
                "geometry": mapping(gap_geom)
            })
    elif family == "line":
        dg = check_dangle(gdf)
        for i in range(n):
            per_feature[i].extend(dg[i])

    # Report columns computed here, then assigned onto gdf itself
    # instead of building each feature's properties dict from scratch
    # (an earlier version did that, discarding every other original
    # column the uploaded file had — a real difference from
    # geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd, which has always preserved
    # them). "name" is guaranteed present by the caller already.
    names = gdf["name"]
    error_types, has_errors, partners, metrics, severities = [], [], [], [], []
    for i in range(n):
        errs = per_feature[i]
        has_error = len(errs) > 0
        partner_idx = errs[0][1] if has_error and isinstance(errs[0][1], int) else None
        error_types.append(errs[0][0] if has_error else "")
        has_errors.append(has_error)
        partners.append(str(names.iloc[partner_idx]) if partner_idx is not None else "")
        metrics.append(round(errs[0][2], 6) if has_error else 0)
        severities.append("error" if has_error else "")

    gdf["error_type"] = error_types
    gdf["has_error"] = has_errors
    gdf["partner"] = partners
    gdf["metric"] = metrics
    gdf["severity"] = severities

    # A None in an ORIGINAL column (not under our control) would
    # otherwise vanish silently once this result is serialized to
    # JSON, instead of showing up as an empty value.
    for col in gdf.columns:
        if col != "geometry":
            gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

    # Kept as two separate collections instead of one concatenated
    # list (an earlier version merged them): a gap is synthetic — it
    # has no corresponding row in the uploaded file — and merging it
    # in inflated the feature count on a dense test file to 54 rows
    # for 10 real features (44 pairwise "gap" candidates), with no way
    # for the map to show just the original data or for the count to
    # distinguish "real feature" from "synthetic gap". JS puts each
    # collection on its own map source (topology-py / topology-gaps-py)
    # instead. Gaps stay a fixed, small property set (unlike the real
    # features above) — a gap has no original row to inherit columns
    # from, it's purely computed.
    return {
        "features": gdf.__geo_interface__,
        "gaps": {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": extra_features}
    }

import geopandas as gpd

# The sliver/gap thresholds above (and every check_*() function) work
# in gdf's OWN coordinate units — "Gap search distance (degrees)" in
# the panel only means what it says if gdf is actually in a geographic
# CRS — so read_upload() reprojecting to WGS84 is what makes them right,
# before any check runs, not just before the map draws it.
gdf, original_crs, crs_warning, _ = read_upload()
if gdf is not None:
    if "name" not in gdf.columns:
        gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

def export_crs(g):
    # Reprojects `g` back to the CRS it was uploaded in — used by the
    # download button below, so what comes out matches what went in
    # even though the checks above always run in WGS84.
    if g is None or original_crs is None or original_crs == "EPSG:4326":
        return g
    return g.to_crs(original_crs)

# No built-in fallback anymore (an earlier version diagnosed two
# hardcoded example polygons automatically whenever nothing had been
# uploaded) — see geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's identical change:
# the page now starts genuinely empty until the user either uploads a
# file or clicks "Load example" below, so "no results yet" actually
# means no results yet.
EMPTY_FC = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}
if gdf is not None:
    result = detect_and_check(gdf, sliver_threshold=sliverThreshold, gap_proximity=gapProximity)
    result["originalCrsFeatures"] = export_crs(gdf).__geo_interface__
    result["crsWarning"] = crs_warning
else:
    result = {"features": EMPTY_FC, "gaps": EMPTY_FC, "originalCrsFeatures": EMPTY_FC, "crsWarning": None}
result
```

```{.webgeods-python #topology-export-shp-py .tool-cell}
# Only run on demand (see downloadButton below), not on every check:
# re-exports gdf (the just-checked features, already available from
# topology-diagnose-py above) reprojected back to the CRS the file
# was UPLOADED in, as an actual shapefile (geopandas.to_file()), zips
# the resulting .shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj/.cpg in memory, and returns it
# base64-encoded -- same pattern as geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's
# geometry-export-shp-py.
import base64
import io
import os
import zipfile

export_crs(gdf).to_file("/tmp/webgeods_export.shp", driver="ESRI Shapefile")

buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for fname in sorted(os.listdir("/tmp")):
        if fname.startswith("webgeods_export."):
            with open(f"/tmp/{fname}", "rb") as f:
                z.writestr(fname.replace("webgeods_export", "result"), f.read())

base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")
```
